plus.analyst_notes:
Closes https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/issues/23246
Crypto-theft coding convention used throughout this batch: stolen funds coded as confidentiality data variety Virtual currency (data_victim Victim organization unless customer wallets were drained), integrity Fraudulent transaction for the unauthorized transfers, and the USD loss in impact (Asset and fraud). Template Hacking-ext-unknown used, with asset S - Unknown and vector Unknown (no entry method known; the exchange's wallets were targeted, not a web app). Actor coded Unknown, not external Nation-state: Grinex blames 'foreign intelligence agencies' but Chainalysis disputes this and raises a possible insider/false-flag scenario. Hacking is kept as the action because the only account of events is a cyber-attack; reviewer may change if a later source confirms an insider. Actor block uses 'unknown' orientation.
Data: customer funds (1 billion rubles, about $13.2M) -> Virtual currency, data_victim Customer; impact $13.2M.
Victim: Grinex, KG; NAICS 523999 (issue tag 52). Headcount Unknown. Only one source (Infosecurity Magazine) in the issue.
Timeline: attack 'last week' relative to the April 2026 article -> 2026-04, dbir_year 2027.

event_chain.summary: Access to exchange wallets, method not disclosed

summary: In April 2026 sanctioned Kyrgyzstan-based crypto exchange Grinex, believed to be the successor of Garantex, suspended operations after what it called a large-scale cyber-attack that stole about one billion rubles ($13.2 million) from Russian customers. Grinex blamed Western intelligence agencies, but Chainalysis noted the stolen stablecoins were quickly swapped into TRX through a Tron DEX previously used by Garantex and suggested the theft may have been a false flag covering an insider move of funds.
